A1.justification: Both complete 16-page PDFs describe Rotated Runtime Smooth, with matching main sections, references, and Appendix A. Text and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of all content.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization evaluations, commonsense QA results, group-size ablations, kernel benchmarks, and activation analyses and simulations in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–4, kernel measurements in Figure 6, and Appendix A analyses and simulations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain identical Runtime Smooth and Rotated Runtime Smooth procedures, including reordering, group-wise smoothing, kernel fusion, rotation, and quantization.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WikiText-2, ARC-e, ARC-c, BoolQ, and OBQA evaluations. Appendix A retains the same activation populations and synthetic spike-outlier scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3, including FP16, RTN, SmoothQuant, GPTQ, QuaRot, and SpinQuant where applicable. Figure 6 retains the same per-channel and sub-channel kernel baselines.

E3.justification: Both versions retain identical model configurations, quantization schemes, metrics, group sizes, and kernel evaluation settings. Section 4.1 specifies the same calibration set of 128 WikiText-2 samples with sequence length 2048.

E4.justification: The preliminary smoothing ablation in Figure 3, group-size study in Table 4, and Appendix A outlier simulations and analyses in Figures 7–9 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including the Monte Carlo discussion in Appendix A.1 and error bars in Figure 8. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-test information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results, and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports QuaRot/RRS perplexities of 57.33/6.66 for LLaMA3-70B under A4W4KV16 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning in Sections 2–3, Equations (1)–(4), and the multiple-spike derivation in Appendix A.1, Equations (5)–(10), are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free activation smoothing, handling channel-wise and spike outliers, negligible overhead, and improved INT4 accuracy.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are unchanged. Both retain the model-sensitivity discussion and Appendix A.1's qualification that activations with only two outlier tokens can trouble RRS.

D1.justification: Implementation and calibration details, group sizes, RTX 4070 Ti/NVBench information, and the project-page link are identical. No reproducibility or resource-access information changes.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to smoothing, rotation, and training-based methods are unchanged, including Section 5.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025' to 'Preprint. Under review.' The arXiv stamp changes from v1/30 Sep 2024 to v2/11 Nov 2024. Body wording, title, authors, and document organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–4 retain identical graphics, captions, formatting, and placement. Pagination and page layout are unchanged; the header and version-stamp differences are wording substitutions.

improvement.justification: Both versions provide identical scientific content, experimental evidence, mathematical analysis, limitations, and reproducibility information, including the appendices. The publication-status and version/date text updates do not materially improve or weaken the paper.
